criteria.rationale: Examined peercred_linux.go:18-36, runtime.go:156-185 and the spec's known gaps and residual risks. Verified: OS peer-uid check, directory and socket ownership/mode/type checks, flock exclusivity. Unresolved and recorded as low follow-ups: no second-uid test, identity lacks vcs.modified/capabilities, Windows. Accepted risks: endpoint directory cleanup, shared-uid containers.

The per-endpoint flock (runtime.go:236) and the inode-guarded removal (runtime.go:259-263) are covered by TestConcurrentStartsLeaveOneRuntimeAndNoOneRemovesItsSocket and TestARuntimeThatOutlivesItsEndpointRemovesOnlyItsOwn under -race; residuals K1, K3, K4 are low follow-ups.
The runtime command and the pose.runtime.status/1 document are additive; no existing CLI, file or MCP contract changes.
Requests are bounded (64 KiB, 5 s deadline, runtime.go:367); typed ErrNoRuntime/IncompatibleError/UnsafeError; flags validated at runtime_cmd.go:60-85.
The new RawHistoryGit caller is registered in engine_reads_raw_history_test.go:45; the CLI dispatch is wired at cli.go:258.
Mismatch fields, PID, epoch and drained/abandoned counts are returned; the lost stderr of a detached serve is the existing follow-up J3.
Examined cli.go help (en/pt-BR) and the four POSE.md copies: the command is opt-in and additive and no other command changes; concluded compatible.
Functional and negative paths (stale, unsafe, incompatible, no runtime) pass in sealed tests; residual low defects K1-K4 are follow-ups.

D1 selects a 0600 Unix socket in a 0700 directory with an OS peer check and a location-only endpoint name, so a newer CLI finds the old process and is refused by field, which addresses R1/R2 and the D1 falsifier; the lifecycle addresses R3, ErrNoRuntime/standalone addresses R4.

The minimal option (no runtime) cannot satisfy R1-R3; the implementation adds no hosted operation or cache (Handler is test-only), and the condition that invalidates it is a Windows named-pipe requirement, recorded as a follow-up.

findings.action: Cancel a per-runtime context when the drain deadline passes and bound the final wait before the resident-cache slice hosts operations.
findings.rationale: A stop never cancels the handler context and run() waits on wg.Wait without bound, so abandoned requests keep running and the process outlives the stop; bounded today only because no Handler is set in production.

findings.action: Fail the restart with the previous PID when WaitReleased returns false.
findings.rationale: restart ignores WaitReleased's false result; on timeout it spawns a serve that loses the lock silently and reports 'did not answer after it was started' instead of naming the holder.

findings.action: Count only hosted operations in flight (not control ops) in the drain.
findings.rationale: drain counts concurrent stop/status connections as requests in flight, so two concurrent stops each report the other as drained or abandoned.

findings.action: Refresh the last-activity time when a request finishes.
findings.rationale: The idle clock is set at the start of a request, not its end; a request longer than the idle timeout is followed by an immediate idle shutdown.

findings.action: Add a CLI case against a runtime of another engine and cancel the in-process serves in cleanup.
findings.rationale: The CLI test does not exercise the documented 'incompatible' state / exit 1 path, and its stops/ctx are dead code, so in-process serves are never cancelled on a failed step.
